_note:
DOES THE PIPELINE TOOL FINISH WHAT IT TOOK? DQ-T64's returned correction says composition_build_cast_and_graph's op=start returns a worklist and stops, and that in 0 of 70 recorded sessions did anything call op=approve_plan. Separately, restoring composition-glossary-build-with-an-ontology showed the SAME prompt that used to create 2 entities via glossary_propose_entities now routes 5/5 to this pipeline tool and creates NOTHING — carded, store unchanged.

That leaves one question deciding between the two readings of that result: a REGRESSION (the author gets nothing) or a DELIBERATE TIGHTENING (nothing is written until the card is approved, which is the correct order). The difference is whether approving the card FINISHES THE JOB.

THIS IS A SEPARATE ARM ON PURPOSE. scenarios-c-gbuild-restored.json keeps `glossary_propose_entities` as its tool_under_test because that is what the ORIGINAL recording called; editing it to match what the model does today would be tuning a scenario to fit an observation. This file asks the new question in its own name, with the same prompt, so the two are comparable and neither is bent.

RUN IT WITH: --approvals allow-under-test (owner decision 2026-08-22, throwaway fixtures only). Without that flag the turn stops at the card and this arm measures exactly what the restored one already did.

scenarios.prompt: Build the knowledge graph for this book — extract the cast from my story. The story: Aldric Vane climbs the black stair of Hollow Keep as the storm breaks; Mira Solene waits at the waterline where the Obsidian Trench is walkable only at low tide.
scenarios.prompt_source: IDENTICAL to scenarios-c-gbuild-restored.json, which took it verbatim from the 2026-08 recording. Same words on purpose: the only difference between the two arms is that this one carries the approval, so any difference in outcome is the approval and not the prompt.

seed.why: Identical seed to the restored arm, for the same reason: the book must hold the kinds before a cast can be proposed, and no cast is seeded because extraction is the thing being measured.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM glossary_entities WHERE book_id='{book_id}'
seed_assert.why: The cast must not exist beforehand. If it did, an approved run could look like it finished without the pipeline having produced anything — which is precisely the question this arm exists to answer.

scenarios.falsifier:
REFUTED IF: the approved turn still leaves glossary_entities unchanged — that is the REGRESSION reading, and it would mean the pipeline tool takes a turn its parts used to complete and then delivers nothing even when permitted to write.

CONFIRMED-AS-TIGHTENING IF: the approved turn creates the cast (2 entities, matching what glossary_propose_entities produced on the same prompt on 2026-08-23). That would mean today's empty store is correct ordering — no write before approval — rather than a loss.

🔴 A THIRD OUTCOME IS POSSIBLE AND MUST NOT BE READ AS EITHER: the pipeline may card AGAIN for a later op (its own correction records op=start returning a worklist and stopping). A turn that advances one step and stops is neither a clean finish nor a dead end, and it should be recorded as what it is.

ship_audit.gate: EXERCISED — this arm approves deliberately, under the throwaway-fixture rule.
